plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Fields of towering golden-yellow blooms with dark, seed-packed centers turn their faces across the Kansas plains. Whole fields glow like a sea of small suns at the end of summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer, peaking from late August to mid-September in Kansas
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is really hundreds to thousands of tiny individual flowers, called florets, packed into a spiral pattern. Young sunflower buds track the sun across the sky each day.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: This low, wiry shrub covers upland moors in waves of purple and pink. Its tiny bell-shaped blooms hum with bees and give the hills of Britain their late-summer color.
plants.location: Moorlands and heaths of Britain and northern Europe
plants.funFact: Heather moorlands are tended by rotational burning and grazing, and they support specialist wildlife such as red grouse. Bees make a dark, richly flavored heather honey from the nectar.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Australia's national floral emblem bursts into fluffy, fragrant golden pom-poms as winter ends in the Southern Hemisphere. Each puff is a cluster of 40 to 80 tiny flowers, and together they brighten the bush with sunshine.
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including South Australia and Victoria
plants.funFact: Golden wattle's gold and green match Australia's national sporting colors. National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.
